# casdoor_key (Resource)

Manages a Casdoor key, an access key and secret that calls the Casdoor API on behalf of an organization, an application or a user.

Only the attributes set in the configuration are written to Casdoor. The other fields of the object, including the ones not listed here, keep their current values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "casdoor_key" "ci" {
  owner        = casdoor_organization.acme.name
  name         = "ci"
  display_name = "CI key"
  type         = "Organization"
  organization = casdoor_organization.acme.name
  state        = "Active"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the key, unique within its owner.
- `owner` (String) The organization that the object belongs to.

### Optional

- `access_key` (String) The access key.
- `access_secret` (String, Sensitive) The access secret.
- `application` (String) The application that the key belongs to.
- `display_name` (String) The display name.
- `expire_time` (String) The time when the key expires, in the RFC 3339 format.
- `organization` (String) The organization that the key belongs to.
- `state` (String) The state, e.g. `Active`.
- `type` (String) What the key belongs to: `Organization`, `Application`, `User` or `General`.
- `user` (String) The user that the key belongs to.

### Read-Only

- `created_time` (String) The time when the key was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of the key in the `owner/name` format.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the organization and the name.
terraform import casdoor_key.example <organization>/<name>
```
